model.architecture: Liquid AI hybrid conv-attention decoder (LFM2 ShortConv + attention); reasoning variant that works problems inside <think>...</think>, thought channel declared in bundle metadata

session_defaults.notes: Card: give it a generous token budget (>=2048) - a reasoning model truncated mid-thought produces no final answer; Gallery guidance is to set max tokens high (2048-4096), and size --max-num-tokens so thinking turns complete.

variants.quantization: int4 blockwise-32 + OCTAV linears, int8 embedding, convs float

recommended.reason: ~1.7x faster than int8 on a Pixel 8a CPU and 41% smaller

platform_notes: Requires litert-lm >= 0.15 / a recent AI Edge Gallery (the 2026-10-13 re-pack uses the lfm2 model type, which 0.14 does not have); files were updated in place 2026-08-04 to add the ExecutorMetadata section litert-lm >= 0.15 requires (weights and graph byte-identical)
In the Gallery select the CPU backend and set max tokens high (2048-4096)
First device load compiles the graph and can take about a minute; later loads are instant

known_issues: Cannot create a GPU engine: pre-0.9.2 ShortConv export carries INT64 ADD/CAST, GATHER_ND and a const-input GREATER_EQUAL; the GPU delegate takes 536 of 579 ops and the runtime refuses the partial split - use the CPU backend (the _int4_gpu file is the GPU re-export)

Multi-turn (3-turn probe on the int8 file, litert-lm 0.17.0, 2026-09-15; not re-run on this file): the runtime removes past turns' reasoning from the history before each turn (the 0.15.0 form is gone) and the int8 file answers the previous question at turn 3 with the default setting; the bf16 model passes with LiquidAI's template, which keeps only the most recent turn's reasoning (runs: LiteRT-LM #3184). Start a fresh conversation per task, on a new Engine (LiteRT-LM #3165)

Create a new Engine for each conversation — on litert-lm 0.18.0 the runtime starts a new Conversation on an Engine that already ran another conversation from the earlier conversation's short-convolution state, reusing the prompt tokens the two conversations share and not resetting the state (LiteRT-LM #3165); a probe asking three questions first in a pirate-persona conversation and then in a conversation told to answer in one word (CPU backend, also for the _gpu files; litert-lm 0.18.0 on a Mac) could not measure any of the four files, because it caps each answer at 200 tokens and this model answers after its reasoning.

Thinking cannot be switched off on litert-lm 0.18.0: ThinkingConfig(enable_thinking=False) has no effect on this file (the model still reasons in the thought channel, fills a 400-token cap with it and gives no answer text; measured 2026-10-12); set thinking_token_budget (300 answered 17 × 23 under a 700-token cap) and a cap above it.

Re-packed 2026-10-13, metadata only (llm_model_type lfm2, and the chat template now renders tool calls and tool results; weights, tokenizer and graph byte-identical): on litert-lm 0.18.0 the LFM2 tool call is parsed (tool_calls, automatic_tool_calling) and the tool result reaches the model (measured 2026-10-13). The lfm2 model type needs litert-lm >= 0.15.0 (0.14 has no lfm2 type); on 0.15-0.17 the call still arrives as text. The floor is read from the LiteRT-LM source, not run.

variants.quantization: same int4 recipe and weights as the int4 file (int4 blockwise-32 + OCTAV linears, int8 embedding, convs float), re-exported with litert-torch 0.9.3 + litert-converter 0.3.1 so it runs on the GPU

platform_notes: GPU needs litert-lm >= 0.16.0 (verified by generation on Android OpenCL and macOS, not just by a benchmark table); the Gallery bundles its own runtime which may lag that version - if its GPU toggle fails there, use CPU
On iOS Metal set maxNumTokens to 1024; for a thinking model budget the context so the thinking phase completes

Includes the ExecutorMetadata section litert-lm >= 0.15 needs
